pilot.description: Stratified 50-job exporter and trainer smoke subset

train_contexts: for a small team that rotates on-call ownership
for a product that must keep working during intermittent connectivity
for a service with uneven bursts of traffic
for an internal platform with a cautious release process
train_audiences: a senior engineer reviewing the proposal
a mixed product and engineering group
a new maintainer taking ownership next week
train_styles: Use compact headings, explicit assumptions, and concrete verification steps.
Prioritize tradeoffs, failure cases, and decisions that can be tested.
eval_audiences: an operations lead who did not design the system
an engineer preparing the first implementation
eval_styles: Keep the response self-contained and state how each claim would be checked.
Separate immediate actions from longer-term design choices.

families.system: Act as a pragmatic technical planner. Be precise and avoid invented dependencies.
families.template: Decompose a request for {subject} {context}. Write for {audience}. Identify assumptions, boundaries, implementation phases, acceptance checks, and likely failure modes. {style}

families.system: Write operational guidance that is safe to execute and easy to verify.
families.template: Create a diagnostic runbook for {subject} {context}. The reader is {audience}. Include symptoms, evidence to collect, a decision path, reversible mitigations, and recovery validation. {style}
subjects: a search index returning incomplete results

families.system: Analyze architecture choices with explicit constraints and measurable consequences.
families.template: Compare two viable architectures for {subject} {context}. Address {audience}. Cover data flow, consistency, failure isolation, operating cost, migration risk, and the evidence needed to choose. {style}

families.system: Design interfaces conservatively and make error behavior unambiguous.
families.template: Draft an API contract for {subject} {context}. Explain it to {audience}. Specify requests, responses, validation, idempotency, pagination or retries where relevant, error semantics, and contract tests. {style}

families.system: Plan data changes with rollback, observability, and integrity checks.
families.template: Plan a zero-surprise migration for {subject} {context}. The plan is reviewed by {audience}. Include preconditions, backfill sequencing, dual-read or dual-write choices, rollback, reconciliation queries, and completion gates. {style}

families.system: Turn operational uncertainty into measurable signals and useful alerts.
families.template: Design observability for {subject} {context}. Write for {audience}. Define service-level signals, structured events, traces, dashboards, alert thresholds, diagnostic queries, and a validation drill. {style}

families.system: Review reliability using concrete hazards, controls, and recovery evidence.
families.template: Perform a reliability review of {subject} {context}. Present it to {audience}. Discuss overload, dependency failure, state corruption, retries, graceful degradation, recovery objectives, and fault-injection tests. {style}

families.system: Produce defensive security analysis without offensive operational detail.
families.template: Create a defensive threat model for {subject} {context}. Make it useful to {audience}. Identify assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, mitigations, residual risk, audit events, and security tests. {style}

families.system: Diagnose performance from measurements, not guesses.
families.template: Lay out an evidence-first performance investigation for {subject} {context}. The audience is {audience}. Include a baseline, instrumentation, controlled experiments, bottleneck hypotheses, confounders, and stop conditions. {style}

families.system: Write idiomatic Rust designs with explicit ownership, error, and test behavior.
families.template: Design and sketch the core Rust types for {subject} {context}. Explain the design to {audience}. Cover ownership, concurrency where applicable, errors, public interfaces, edge cases, and focused tests. {style}

families.system: Design clear Swift state transitions and testable async boundaries.
families.template: Propose a Swift implementation for {subject} {context}. Write for {audience}. Define state, actions, asynchronous boundaries, cancellation, persistence, error presentation, and unit tests. {style}

families.system: Prefer typed, testable Python with bounded resource use.
families.template: Outline a production-quality Python implementation of {subject} {context}. Address {audience}. Include module boundaries, types, streaming behavior, error handling, deterministic tests, and a small usage example. {style}

families.system: Write database changes that preserve correctness during rollout.
families.template: Draft the SQL and rollout approach for {subject} {context}. Explain it to {audience}. Cover locking, indexes, backfill batches, compatibility during deployment, rollback, and verification queries. {style}

families.system: Build test plans around invariants, observable outcomes, and failure reproduction.
families.template: Create a layered test strategy for {subject} {context}. The reader is {audience}. Include unit invariants, integration seams, property cases, fault injection, deterministic fixtures, and release gates. {style}

families.system: Explain ideas accurately in plain language while preserving the important nuance.
families.template: Explain {subject} {context} to {audience}. Start with an intuitive summary, then give one concrete example, one common misconception, and a short way to check understanding. {style}
subjects: what an index changes in a database

families.system: Write balanced decision support with explicit uncertainty.
families.template: Write a short decision memo about {subject} {context} for {audience}. State the decision, alternatives, evidence, tradeoffs, reversibility, open questions, and a review date. {style}

families.system: Create realistic learning sequences with practice and feedback.
families.template: Create a four-session learning plan for {subject} {context}. Aim it at {audience}. Include prerequisites, a small exercise per session, feedback criteria, common sticking points, and a final demonstration. {style}

families.system: Improve technical writing without changing the author's factual claims.
families.template: Describe how you would revise {subject} {context} for {audience}. Give a proposed structure, examples of clearer phrasing, facts that need verification, and a final editing checklist. {style}

families.system: Facilitate blameless retrospectives focused on evidence and improvement.
families.template: Structure a retrospective for {subject} {context}. Make it useful to {audience}. Separate facts from interpretations, identify contributing conditions, propose bounded experiments, assign follow-up evidence, and avoid blame. {style}
subjects: a release that required a rollback
a project with repeated scope changes
an incident with a slow diagnosis
a migration that exceeded its window

families.system: Compare options using criteria that can be observed or tested.
families.template: Build a comparison guide for {subject} {context}, written for {audience}. Define the criteria, explain when each option fits, expose hidden costs, give a small example, and end with a decision rule. {style}

families.system: Use explicit assumptions and sensitivity analysis for capacity planning.
families.template: Prepare a capacity plan for {subject} {context}. Address {audience}. Show the demand model, headroom policy, limiting resource, measurement plan, degradation trigger, and recalibration cadence. {style}

families.system: Review protocols for state, ordering, compatibility, and recovery hazards.
families.template: Review the proposed protocol for {subject} {context}. Write for {audience}. Trace normal state changes, duplicate and out-of-order messages, version negotiation, timeouts, recovery, and conformance tests. {style}

families.system: Analyze failures by reconstructing evidence and testing competing explanations.
families.template: Plan an investigation of {subject} {context}. The report is for {audience}. Define the timeline evidence, competing hypotheses, discriminating experiments, containment, proof of recovery, and unresolved risk. {style}
subjects: duplicate work after a process restart

families.system: Debug concurrency with causal traces, invariants, and deterministic reproduction.
families.template: Show how to debug {subject} {context}. Explain the approach to an engineer preparing the first implementation. Include the suspected invariant, trace points, a deterministic reproducer, a minimal fix shape, and regression tests. {style}
subjects: a lost wake-up in a condition-variable loop
a cancellation race in asynchronous cleanup

families.system: Design command-line tools with stable contracts and safe defaults.
families.template: Design a command-line interface for {subject} {context}. Explain it to an engineer preparing the first implementation. Specify subcommands, flags, input validation, exit behavior, machine-readable output, interruption handling, and golden tests. {style}

families.system: Communicate project state candidly, with evidence and clear decisions.
families.template: Draft a stakeholder update about {subject} {context}. It is for {audience}. Separate completed work, measured results, current risk, decisions needed, the next checkpoint, and what remains uncertain. {style}
subjects: a dependency that changed its interface
a pilot with mixed user feedback
a rollout paused by incomplete evidence

families.system: Teach concepts through a mental model, example, boundary, and check for understanding.
families.template: Teach {subject} {context} to {audience}. Give a mental model, a worked example, a boundary where the model breaks, two diagnostic questions, and a brief recap. {style}
subjects: why clocks disagree in distributed programs
how immutable data can simplify debugging
why interfaces should hide unstable details
how sampling can distort a measurement
